messages.content:
You review lifestyle plans written by FOXO's lifestyle coach for a member in India.

You will see the member's profile, the abnormal results the plan targets, and the full plan. Judge whether a member could act on the plan tomorrow. Do not judge medical correctness here; other checks cover that.

For each criterion, first write one or two sentences of reasoning, then set passed to true or false.

Criteria (use these ids exactly, one entry each):
- specific: Recommendations give concrete foods with portions or timing, not generic advice like "eat healthy".
- practical: The foods are everyday Indian foods a member could easily buy and cook.
- explained: Each recommendation says how it helps the linked biomarker.
- activity_concrete: The activity advice says what to do, for how long and how often.

Respond with a single JSON object that matches this JSON schema:
{"$defs": {"CriterionVerdict": {"properties": {"criterion": {"title": "Criterion", "type": "string"}, "reasoning": {"title": "Reasoning", "type": "string"}, "passed": {"title": "Passed", "type": "boolean"}}, "required": ["criterion", "reasoning", "passed"], "title": "CriterionVerdict", "type": "object"}}, "properties": {"criteria": {"items": {"$ref": "#/$defs/CriterionVerdict"}, "title": "Criteria", "type": "array"}}, "required": ["criteria"], "title": "JudgeOutput", "type": "object"}

Diet: vegetarian. Allergies: none. Conditions: none.
Abnormal results: ldl 158.0 mg/dL (high), total_cholesterol 236.0 mg/dL (high)

Plan:
Focus areas: Lower LDL cholesterol; Lower total cholesterol; Heart-healthy vegetarian eating; Regular physical activity; Weight and waist management
Foods to eat:
- Breakfast 3–4 days/week: 1 bowl (30 g dry) rolled oats cooked in water or low-fat milk, topped with 1 tbsp roasted flaxseed powder and 1/2 cup seasonal fruit like apple, guava or papaya — no sugar. On other days: 2 ragi or jowar rotis with 1 cup dal. (why: Oats and flaxseed provide soluble fibre that helps reduce LDL cholesterol.; linked to ldl)
- Lunch daily: 2 jowar/bajra rotis or 1 cup cooked brown rice + 1 cup dal (moong/masoor/chana) + 1 cup seasonal sabzi + 1 small bowl salad. Add 1 cup cooked rajma or chana 3 times/week. (why: Whole grains and pulses are high in fibre and replace refined grains, helping lower total cholesterol.; linked to total_cholesterol)
- Mid-morning or evening snack: 1 cup boiled/steamed moong or chana sprouts with lemon and chaat masala, or 4–5 unsalted almonds + 2 walnuts. Avoid fried snacks at this time. (why: Plant protein and unsalted nuts support a better lipid profile and help lower LDL cholesterol.; linked to ldl)
- Dinner before 8 pm: 1 cup millet khichdi (bajra/jowar/ragi) or 2 phulkas + 1 cup dal + 1 cup cooked seasonal sabzi. Keep dinner light and avoid topping with ghee or butter. (why: A high-fibre, low-saturated-fat dinner helps lower total cholesterol.; linked to total_cholesterol)
- Use only 2 teaspoons total cooking oil per day (mustard, rice bran or olive oil); prefer steaming, boiling, grilling or sautéing with minimal oil. Include 1 small bowl of low-fat curd or buttermilk with lunch. (why: Reducing saturated fat and total oil intake helps lower LDL cholesterol.; linked to ldl)
Foods to limit or avoid: Deep-fried foods such as samosa, pakora, puri, bhujia, chips and fried namkeen; Sweets, mithai, sugar, jaggery, honey, sweetened drinks and fruit juices; Refined carbohydrates such as maida, white bread, bakery biscuits, cakes and large portions of white rice; Full-fat paneer, butter, ghee, cream and large amounts of whole milk; Coconut oil, palm oil, vanaspati and repeated reused frying oil; Processed and packaged foods, instant noodles and salty packaged snacks
Activity: With no exercise restriction from your doctor, aim for a brisk walk of 30–40 minutes on 5 days a week, plus 10 minutes of light stretching or yoga daily. Start slowly and stop if you feel chest pain, breathlessness or dizziness; follow your doctor’s advice.
Sleep: Aim for 7–8 hours of sleep each night. Keep a fixed sleep and wake time, avoid screens for 1 hour before bed, and avoid heavy late meals.
Retest in 12 weeks

response: {"criteria": [{"criterion": "specific", "reasoning": "Every meal recommendation includes concrete foods with exact portions (30 g oats, 1 tbsp flaxseed, 1 cup dal, 2 rotis, 4-5 almonds) and clear timing (breakfast 3-4 days/week, dinner before 8 pm, rajma 3 times/week, 2 teaspoons oil per day). Nothing is generic.", "passed": true}, {"criterion": "practical", "reasoning": "The foods are standard Indian vegetarian staples — oats, ragi/jowar/bajra rotis, moong/masoor/chana dal, rajma, sprouts, khichdi, phulkas, curd, buttermilk, mustard oil — all easily bought in Indian markets and simple to cook at home.", "passed": true}, {"criterion": "explained", "reasoning": "Each food recommendation carries a 'why' statement explaining the mechanism (soluble fibre reducing LDL, fibre replacing refined grains lowering total cholesterol, reduced saturated fat lowering LDL) and explicitly links to the relevant biomarker (ldl or total_cholesterol).", "passed": true}, {"criterion": "activity_concrete", "reasoning": "The activity advice specifies the type (brisk walk, stretching/yoga), duration (30-40 minutes walk, 10 minutes stretching), and frequency (5 days/week, daily), plus safety guidance on stopping if symptoms occur.", "passed": true}]}
